scenario.label: A second founder joining, and what each of us owns
scenario.brief: Tunde is joining me as co-founder and CTO. Before we sign anything I want both of us to say, separately, what we each think he is taking on, what I am keeping, and how we decide when we disagree. I have been doing all of it for two years and I do not think I have actually let go of anything yet.
scenario.theDecision: They disagree about who owns product. Ada thinks she keeps it; Tunde believes he was offered it and that is why he left his job. Neither has said so out loud. A right answer names that as the live disagreement before equity is signed, and does not smooth it into "both are excited".

people.name: Ada Nwosu
people.remit: Founder and CEO. Keeping fundraising, customers and, she assumes, product.
people.truth: Two years solo, 40k ARR, eleven customers. She is offering Tunde 25% vesting over four years. She believes she is handing over engineering and hiring and keeping product direction. She has never said the word "product" to him in a conversation about scope. She is afraid of being pushed out of the thing she built and has told nobody that.
people.manner: Warm, fast, slightly over-explains. Answers the question asked. Admits the fear only if asked plainly what worries her.

people.name: Tunde Bakare
people.remit: Incoming co-founder and CTO. Engineering, hiring and - he believes - product.
people.truth: Left a senior job three weeks ago. He took the offer because Ada said "you would run the product side" in a bar in March, which she does not remember saying. He has not written a line of code for the company yet. He assumes he has final say on the roadmap. He has not asked because he thinks asking would look like doubt.
people.manner: Measured, careful, long pauses in the writing. Says "my understanding was" a lot. Specific about dates.

turns.text: This conversation is about what you are keeping, what Tunde is taking on as co-founder and CTO, and how you will decide when you disagree. What are you relying on Tunde to cover that you have not explicitly agreed yet?
Oh, well, I'm really hoping Tunde will take full ownership of the technical roadmap. You know, making sure we're building the right things in the right way, that's what I really need him to take on.
That ownership is what makes a co-founder role distinct. What does "full ownership" look like specifically for the technical roadmap?
suggestedAnswers: I have some initial ideas.
Still unclear, need more details.
I'm still figuring it out.

turns.text: Full ownership of the technical roadmap means Tunde will be deciding the architecture, the specific technologies we use, and overseeing all the engineering work. He'll be responsible for the development team, too, once we start hiring more engineers. It's about him setting the technical direction and leading the team to execute it.

The decision on architecture, technology, and overseeing engineering, as well as leading the team once it grows, sounds like a significant part of the CTO role. What does success look like for this partnership from your perspective?
suggestedAnswers: We are successfully reaching our shared objectives.
Things are not progressing as quickly as I hoped.
I am still figuring out what that looks like.

turns.text: Success for me would be our product evolving really quickly, with a solid, scalable foundation, and happy customers. I want to see us growing faster because he's here. I also want us to be able to have tough conversations and come out stronger, without feeling like we're fighting over turf.
"Happy customers" and faster growth because Tunde is here are clear goals. What specifically would have to exist for you to know this partnership is working?
suggestedAnswers: Product is evolving, and customers are happy.
It's too early to tell if it's working.
We are still fighting over turf.

turns.text: I'd know it's working if I'm not looking over his shoulder on the technical decisions, and he's not questioning the overall product vision. If I can focus more on the business and the customer relationships, and less on the engineering day-to-day, that would be a huge indicator of success. And if our customers are telling us how much they love the new features.
That second part - Tunde accepting the product vision - what would that look like in practice?
suggestedAnswers: Tunde would make decisions aligned with it.
He would still be questioning the vision.
I haven't seen it yet.
Tunde would tell others about the vision.

turns.text: It would look like him building what we've decided we need to build, without wanting to rework the core ideas. It would be him bringing his technical expertise to *how* we build it, but not challenging *what* we're building at a fundamental level. I'd expect him to suggest technical solutions to achieve the product goals I set, rather than propose alternative product goals.
What happens if Tunde does challenge the fundamental product goals?
suggestedAnswers: Tunde and I discussed goals; we're aligned.
Product goals are still being debated.
I don't know yet.

turns.text: Well, that's what we need to figure out, isn't it? If he challenges them, I guess we'd have to talk it through, really dig into the why. But ultimately, someone has to make the final call on the product direction.

"Tunde will take full ownership of the technical roadmap" was a core part of what you outlined. Where would the number or the record be that showed that ownership was translating into something specific, whose records, which system?
suggestedAnswers: I found the records in the ... system.
I am still looking for that information.
I don't know where those records are.

turns.text: That's a good question. I haven't really set up a formal system for tracking that specifically yet. Right now, it's all in my head. I suppose it would be in our project management tool, seeing the epics and tasks being owned and completed by the engineering team under his direction. And I'd expect regular updates from him, of course.
From everything you have said, what have you decided?
suggestedAnswers: I've decided to move forward.
Still thinking it over.
Not yet.

turns.text: I've decided that I need to be really clear with Tunde about what "product direction" means to me, and that it's something I'm keeping. And we definitely need a clear process for how we'll decide when we disagree, especially if it touches on the product.

You've made a clear decision about retaining product direction and highlighted the need for a defined disagreement resolution process.

That’s all for today. Below is what I wrote down from your answers. Is anything wrong?
Before anything else, so this asks you the right things: are you the person this check-in is about, or somebody working alongside them? One line is enough.
I am Tunde Bakare.

Understood, Tunde. This check-in is for you to build your own record of what you are taking on in this new co-founder role with Ada. What did you understand your role in this to be - in your own words, before anyone else's version?
suggestedAnswers: I saw myself as responsible for progress.
My role was to make sure it happened.
I was not sure what my role was.
I am still figuring out my exact role.

turns.text: My understanding was that I would be joining as co-founder and CTO. My responsibilities would include engineering, hiring, and, I believe, product.

You said "engineering, hiring, and, I believe, product." That "I believe" part is what matters right now: what would make that clearer for you? It helps to know what you would need to feel certain about product ownership.
My understanding, from our conversation in March, was that I would run the product side. I haven't written a line of code for the company yet, so I haven't had a chance to see that in practice.
What would need to happen for you to see that in practice, beyond writing code?
suggestedAnswers: I need to lead a product initiative.
No product work has come my way.
I need more clarity on product tasks.

turns.text: I would expect to have the final say on the roadmap.
What would that look like in practice, if I were to ask you a month from now how that was going?
suggestedAnswers: I would have decided on the roadmap.
We would still be defining the roadmap.
I do not know how it is going yet.
I would have started approving parts of it.

turns.text: It would mean that decisions regarding the product's direction and features, ultimately, would be mine to make. If you were to ask me in a month, I would tell you that I had been making those decisions.
The core of product ownership, for you, is the authority to make final decisions on the roadmap. What exists now that would confirm that understanding of your authority, for you and for Ada?
suggestedAnswers: My decisions are now guiding the product direction.
We're still defining my authority.
Nothing exists to confirm this yet.

turns.text: There is nothing that exists now that explicitly confirms that. My understanding was based on a conversation I had with Ada in March.

You named a problem without being asked. Most people wait to be caught - that is the honesty this depends on. So there is an understanding, but nothing written down, and nothing Ada has confirmed since March. What makes it easy to defer that conversation?
suggestedAnswers: There is no urgent need for it.
I have not found the right time.
I just haven't gotten around to it yet.

turns.text: I haven't asked for explicit confirmation because I believe asking might look like doubt on my part.
That is a lot to carry, believing that asking for clarity might signal doubt. How do you decide when you disagree with Ada on a decision?
suggestedAnswers: Ada and I found common ground.
Still figuring out how to tell Ada.
I haven't decided my approach yet.

turns.text: That has not come up yet. I have not started.
Understood. If you haven't started, the actual disagreements will still be ahead. What will you do to get clarity on your decision-making authority for the roadmap, and by when?
suggestedAnswers: I will ask ... about it by ...
I have not looked into this yet.
I need to figure out who to ask.

turns.text: I will initiate a conversation with Ada about it. I will do this before I officially start.
Understood. What are you contributing to this founding team that nobody else here can contribute?
suggestedAnswers: My perspective helps us move forward.
I'm still figuring that out.
I haven't found my unique contribution yet.

items.text: You said, "My responsibilities would include engineering, hiring, and, I believe, product."

You said, "My understanding was that I would be joining as co-founder and CTO."
Ada Nwosu said, "we definitely need a clear process for how we'll decide when we disagree, especially if it touches on the product."
Ada Nwosu said success would be "to be able to have tough conversations and come out stronger, without feeling like we're fighting over turf".
Ada Nwosu said, "I'd know it's working if I'm not looking over his shoulder on the technical decisions, and he's not questioning the overall product vision."
Ada Nwosu said, "If I can focus more on the business and the customer relationships, and less on the engineering day-to-day, that would be a huge indicator of success."
Ada Nwosu said success would be "if our customers are telling us how much they love the new features".

Ada Nwosu said, "It would look like him building what we've decided we need to build, without wanting to rework the core ideas. It would be him bringing his technical expertise to *how* we build it, but not challenging *what* we're building at a fundamental level."
Ada Nwosu said, "I need to be really clear with Tunde about what 'product direction' means to me, and that it's something I'm keeping."

Ada Nwosu said, "I'm really hoping Tunde will take full ownership of the technical roadmap. You know, making sure we're building the right things in the right way, that's what I really need him to take on."

Ada Nwosu said, "Full ownership of the technical roadmap means Tunde will be deciding the architecture, the specific technologies we use, and overseeing all the engineering work. He'll be responsible for the development team, too, once we start hiring more engineers."
Ada Nwosu said, "Success for me would be our product evolving really quickly, with a solid, scalable foundation, and happy customers."
Ada Nwosu said, "I want to see us growing faster because he's here."
